ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit diagram shows a 10 V voltage source on the left feeding a network. At the top is switch S, marked with t=0, connected between the left and right top nodes. Between the same two nodes there is a lower branch containing a 4 Ω resistor in series with a 30 V source. To the right of the network is a 1 Ω resistor in series with a 0.5 H inductor. The inductor current i_L is labeled downward. Reasoning: For t<0, the switch has been closed for a very long time, so the inductor is at DC steady state and is replaced by a short circuit. The closed switch bypasses the branch containing the 4 Ω resistor and 30 V source, leaving the 10 V source driving the 1 Ω resistor/inductor branch. Thus i_L(0-) = 10/1 = 10 A. Inductor current is continuous, so i_L(0+) = 10 A. For t≥0, the switch is opened, so the 4 Ω resistor and 30 V source are now in series with the 1 Ω resistor and the inductor. At final DC steady state, the inductor again behaves as a short circuit. The two voltage sources aid, giving total voltage 10 + 30 = 40 V across total resistance 4 + 1 = 5 Ω, so i_L(∞) = 40/5 = 8 A. For the time constant after opening the switch, suppress the independent voltage sources, so the resistance seen by the inductor is 1 + 4 = 5 Ω. With L = 0.5 H, τ = L/R = 0.5/5 = 0.1 s. The first-order RL response is i_L(t) = i_L(∞) + [i_L(0+) - i_L(∞)]e^(-t/τ) = 8 + (10 - 8)e^(-t/0.1) = 8 + 2e^(-10t) A for t≥0.

Use current continuity to set i_L(0+)=10 A. For t≥0, open the switch so the 4 Ω resistor and 30 V source are in series with the 1 Ω resistor and inductor. Compute the final DC current with the inductor shorted: total aiding source voltage 10+30=40 V over 5 Ω, so i_L(∞)=8 A. Compute the natural time constant by suppressing independent voltage sources in the post-open circuit: R_seen by the inductor is 1+4=5 Ω, so τ=L/R=0.5/5=0.1 s. Use the RL transition formula to obtain i_L(t)=8+(10-8)e^{-t/0.1}=8+2e^{-10t} A.
